title: Update Delayed Shipment Priority Levels
prompt: A logistics company tracks shipments through various milestones. Management wants to automatically escalate the priority level of shipments that are currently delayed. A shipment is considered delayed if its actual_delivery_date is NULL (not yet delivered) AND the current date (assume '2024-01-15') is more than 2 days past its scheduled_delivery_date. Write a DO block that updates the priority_level column in the shipments table: set it to 'critical' if current priority is 'high', set it to 'high' if current priority is 'standard', and leave 'critical' unchanged. After the DO block, write a SELECT statement that returns all columns from the shipments table ordered by shipment_id ascending.
schema_ddl: CREATE TABLE shipments (shipment_id INT PRIMARY KEY, tracking_number VARCHAR(20), origin_city VARCHAR(50), destination_city VARCHAR(50), scheduled_delivery_date DATE, actual_delivery_date DATE, priority_level VARCHAR(20), carrier VARCHAR(30));

composite_moves: identify delayed shipments using date comparison and NULL check
conditionally update priority_level based on current value

hints: You need to identify which shipments are delayed by comparing dates and checking delivery status.
A delayed shipment has no actual delivery date and is more than 2 days past its scheduled date relative to 2024-01-15.

Use a DO block to update priority_level with conditional logic: 'high' becomes 'critical', 'standard' becomes 'high', and 'critical' stays 'critical'. Check the WHERE clause carefully for the date condition.
answer_key:
DO $$
BEGIN
  UPDATE shipments
  SET priority_level = CASE
    WHEN priority_level = 'high' THEN 'critical'
    WHEN priority_level = 'standard' THEN 'high'
    ELSE priority_level
  END
  WHERE actual_delivery_date IS NULL
    AND DATE '2024-01-15' - scheduled_delivery_date > 2;
END $$;

SELECT * FROM shipments ORDER BY shipment_id;
